the role played by trehalose-5-phosphate synthase and trehalose-1-phosphate phosphatase in response to Cd and Cu stress in tobacco plants.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transgenic plants with the lower expression level of the AtTPS synthase gene (B1F) showed the best acclimation to excess Cu and Cd.
transgenic plants with a low level of trehalose synthase activity are more tolerant to Cd and excess of Cu than those with high activity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

trehalose-1-phosphate synthase over-expression in tobacco plants improved tolerance to excess Cu and Cd, and this effect was more evident in the transgenic line with lower trehalose- 6-phosphate synthases expression.
trehalose accumulation is a key factor for the response of plants to oxidative stress.
the AtTPS transgenic tobacco plants showed a better tolerance to Cd and Cu than the WT, probably because of the increased trehalose content, which is a well known stress protectant.

the transgenic plants with the lower expression of AtTPS1 are the most tolerant to excess Cu and Cd.
trehalose-1,6-bisphosphate synthase (TPS) overexpression in tobacco plants confers tolerance to Cd and Cu excess.
